question: The term 'slip' is related to which of the following games?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cricket**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term 'slip' in cricket refers to a fielding position specifically designed to catch balls that are edged by the batsman.
 
• Slip fielders stand behind the batsman on the off side, usually in a line with the wicketkeeper.
 
• These positions are critical for catching balls that deviate slightly after hitting the bat, especially in fast bowling.
 
• The number of slips can vary based on the game situation, ranging from none to as many as four or five.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fielding Positions in Cricket:**

 
 
• **Wicketkeeper:** Positioned directly behind the stumps to catch balls the batsman misses.
 
• **Gully:** Positioned on the off side, typically between slips and point.
 
• **Point:** Positioned square of the wicket on the off side.
 
• **Mid-off:** Positioned straight on the off side, closer to the bowler.
 
 
 
• **Bowling Techniques:**
 
 
• **Fast Bowling:** Involves delivering the ball at high speeds, typically above 140 km/h.
 
• **Spin Bowling:** Involves delivering the ball with a spinning action to deceive the batsman.
 
• **Medium Pace:** Involves delivering the ball at moderate speeds, relying on swing and seam movement.
 
 
 
• **Types of Catches:**
 
 
• **Slip Catch:** Caught by fielders positioned in the slip cordon.
 
• **Outfield Catch:** Caught by fielders positioned in the outfield, typically on the boundary.
 
• **Close-in Catch:** Caught by fielders positioned close to the batsman, such as short leg or silly point.
 
 
 
• **Cricket Formats:**
 
 
• **Test Cricket:** Played over five days with unlimited overs.
 
• **One Day International (ODI):** Limited to 50 overs per side.
 
• **T20 International:** Limited to 20 overs per side.
